### Bible Pathway - June 2, 2011
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathway-june-2-2011.html
Passage: Ezra 3:2-3
Points:
- The returning exiles prioritized worship by rebuilding God's altar before building their own houses.
- Their sacrifices reflected a sincere desire to restore fellowship with God rather than mere ritual.
- Genuine obedience moves believers to surrender material self-reliance and trust entirely in the Lord.
- Committing to God's work attracts spiritual opposition aimed at diverting attention from prayer and Scripture.
- Each believer holds a personal responsibility to complete the work God has ordained.

### Read the Bible: Genesis 3, Matthew 3, Ezra 3, and Acts 3
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/genesis-3-matthew-3-ezra-3-acts-3/
Passage: Ezra 3:1-13
Points:
- The returned exiles were keenly aware of their vulnerability among hostile neighbors.
- Overcoming their fears, they resolutely re-established the altar and reinstated the daily sacrifices prescribed by Moses.
- Laying the temple foundation evoked joyful adoration and renewed confidence in God's covenant promises.
- Elders who remembered Solomon’s temple wept over the comparatively modest scale of the new beginning.
- The community displayed sincere, engaged emotion rather than cynical apathy while pursuing God's will.
